newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, MAY 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, MAY 28.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.

- Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats, who aim to form a coalition government after Ireland's June 6 election, have stretched their lead over the ruling "Rainbow coalition" to eight percentage points, according to an opinion poll for the Irish Independent.
- The Irish economy continues to surge ahead and this year's inflation rate will be lower than expected, the Central Bank of Ireland said.
- Avonmore Foods Plc is adamant that it is not offering too high a price to get Waterford Foods Plc to agree to its merger offer.
- Bertie Ahern, leader of the main opposition Fianna Fail party, has set out new guidelines about how any coalition in which he participates should operate.

- The marching season and next week's resumed multi-party talks will be high on the agenda when Irish Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring and Britain's Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam meet in Dublin on Thursday.
- Ireland's Catholic bishops have repeated their call for a referendum to restore "the constitutional guarantee of the right to life of the unborn child".

- The merger of Waterford Foods and Avonmore Foods should result in savings of more than 10 million pounds in the first year, Avonmore chief executive Pat O'Neill said. Meanwhile, farmer groups opposed to the merger pledged strong opposition to the deal.
- Ireland's Catholic bishops have entered the election fray with a demand for a new abortion referendum.
- The central bank has expressed its concern that soaring house prices will fuel inflation.
- Irish Life Plc sales staff return to work on Wednesday after a bitter 17-week dispute.
